This generator publishes that verification.  It does four things:

assumption_A1_the_marker_is_generated_te.claim: The LEGACY marker is one generated wording emitted for every entry carrying the data field `legacy_subject`, with a second variant for `legacy_principle_transferred` — so the set is DERIVABLE from the data rather than findable by searching prose.

It failed twice: **D-329**, whose PRINCIPLE the [[OI-275]] ruling carried across to the live family design (patched then with a second marker variant, which fixed the instance and left the clause standing everywhere else), and **D-311**, whose subject `chordanalyzer.cpp` `STATUS_ARCHIVE.md:114` records as surviving the engagement and one of whose five produced translation units, `chordsymbolformatter.cpp`, the record arm runs (`notationimplodebridge.cpp:1170`). **The user ruled the clause REMOVED rather than re-argued** — a swept population with two demonstrated errors is not established (#19) — executed in the GENERATOR so one change covers all 80 and cannot drift (#17f). This row carries the full re-verification against a live-reachability test. **[[OI-288]]'s finding may bear on a whole CLASS of them:** the legacy notation arm's reachability turns on one runtime flag defaulting `true` and four branch points, not on compilation, so "dormant" is a statement about a DEFAULT with an enumerated false-negative path, and each verdict must say which it means. NOT in doubt: the marking convention itself (`CLAUDE.md` rule (f), user-ratified 2026-08-02) — what is withdrawn is an unchecked assertion riding along with it | E — verification owed / decisions register | ✅ VERIFIED 2026-08-03 (CC, phase 1w) — the full re-verification is DELIVERED as the generated artifact `tools/audit/decisions/phase1w_legacy_verification.json` (every count, verdict and citation there, none restated; D-431). **0 marks established wrong, so 0 corrected, and the marking convention is NOT in question.** The set is DERIVED, and **five** recorded figures disagree with it — all located, none corrected here (that is action, and this wave gathers). **★ The two results the family design needs. (1) "Dormant" is far weaker than it reads:** NO entry is unreachable at any setting on the notation flag and NONE is dormant-behind-the-default alone — every marked subject with code at HEAD is reached by plain `batch_analyze` (`--joint-inference` defaults OFF), by a batch diagnostic dump flag, or by the test suites. **(2) The largest transfer class was not predicted:** entries a LIVE specification section restates as standing do-not-retry prohibitions, where the mark is RIGHT about the subject and the entry still binds what a future designer may attempt — a third thing a mark can be, which the register has no field for. Both false-negative enumerations in this row are short (the batch diagnostic flags; and `jointKeyWiringEnabled()`, a second default-OFF flag inside the legacy arm). *Historical, preserved (#12): the row was opened saying* "Set size **80**, counted from the data" — *true at phase 1m and stale by one since phase 1n, when D-428 gained the mark; the register's own preamble says 79 and `STATUS.md` + the phase-1m dispatch say 75.* Residues: [[OI-302]] (the third mark class, D-055, and the undetermined transfers), [[OI-303]], [[OI-304]]. **★ AND THE VERDICT ABOVE IS TRUE OF THE POPULATION IT COVERED AND OF NO LARGER ONE — [[OI-354]], opened 2026-08-09.** Entries have carried the legacy mark since this pass ran, and the verification holds no verdict for them; the tool that exists to notice that had been stopping earlier, on a drifted citation, so the growth was invisible. **The ✅ above is NOT withdrawn** — what it verified, it verified — but it must not be read as a statement about the marked set at HEAD | [detail](open_items/OI-289.md) |

source.quote: for each marked entry, is its subject reachable on either production surface at HEAD, and

the_test.half_a_reachability: Is the entry's subject reachable on EITHER production surface at HEAD? Because the notation arm turns on a runtime flag whose default is true rather than on compilation, a bare "dormant" is not an answer: each verdict names WHICH SENSE it means, from the four below.
the_test.half_b_transfer: Does any ruling carry the decision's PRINCIPLE across to the live design, as the OI-275 ruling did for D-329? A mark correct about the subject can still be wrong about the effect.

reachability_senses.production: The subject's code runs on a DEFAULT production path — the in-app record arm, or batch_analyze --joint-inference.
reachability_senses.false-negative-path: Not on any default production path, but reached by an enumerated non-default path: an explicit flag flip, plain batch_analyze (the --joint-inference flag defaults OFF), a batch_analyze diagnostic dump flag, the test suites, or the declared non-production uncached path.
reachability_senses.flag-default-only: Unreachable only while useJointNotationRecord holds its default, and by no other path. (No entry received this verdict — see what_this_found.the_dormancy_is_weaker_than_it_sounds.)
reachability_senses.none: Unreachable at any setting: no code at HEAD implements the subject. A decision whose subject is a prohibition, a closure or a design never built.
reachability_senses.undetermined: The evidence read does not settle it.

transfer_values.ruling-transferred: A later ruling explicitly carried the principle to the live design.
transfer_values.live-prohibition-in-spec: A LIVE specification section restates the decision as a standing do-not-retry. The subject stays legacy; the prohibition binds now.
transfer_values.carried-elsewhere: The record states the doctrine lives on in another, live entry or rule.
transfer_values.assigns-live-work: The decision's OWN text assigns work, ownership or a property to the live design. Not a later ruling — which is why it is a separate value.
transfer_values.explicitly-not-transferred: A ruling states in terms that the decision does NOT bear on the live design.
transfer_values.none-found: The citation scan over every .md/.cpp/.h/.py/.txt surface found no ruling carrying it, and the surfaces that do cite it are register mechanics.
transfer_values.scoped-to-an-act-that-never-ran: A USER RULING settles, on the two records' own words, that the decision's constraint was scoped to an act that was never performed — so no ruling carried it across, and any live-design question that survives is a separate ROWED input rather than a transfer. ADDED 2026-08-09 for Ruling 34; used by one entry. It is a distinct value because the three that could otherwise carry it each say something the ruling declined to say: `none-found` reports a SEARCH result where this is a ruling, `explicitly-not-transferred` asserts the decision does not bear on the live design where the ruling leaves exactly that open, and `undetermined` says the evidence does not settle it where it now does.
transfer_values.undetermined: The evidence read does not settle it.

the_test.how_the_transfer_half_was_searched: Every occurrence of each marked entry's ID was collected across the repository (.md/.cpp/.h/.py/.txt, register-internal data files excluded), and the hits outside the register's own mechanics were read. TWO PROPERTIES OF THE SEARCH, stated because they bound what a "none-found" verdict is worth: (i) it finds a transfer only where the transferring ruling NAMES THE ENTRY — a ruling that carries a principle without citing the decision is invisible to it; (ii) NO marked ID is cited anywhere under src/, so no verdict rests on a code comment.

corrections_made.why: Task 4 licenses correcting a mark this wave ESTABLISHES wrong, on the D-311 precedent. This wave establishes none wrong: on the test the surviving mark actually makes — what the decision is ABOUT — every one of the derived entries is about the dormant pipeline. The one candidate, D-055, turns on a scoping judgment (are the mode-prior preferences themselves legacy-scoped?) that is not a code fact, so it is reported and the mark stands.
corrections_made.convention_in_question: NO. Task 4's last clause fires if the failure rate puts the marking convention in question; the failure rate is zero. What the wave found instead is about what a mark does NOT say, which is the thing the 2026-08-03 weakening already ruled.

what_this_found.the_dormancy_is_weaker_than_it_sounds: No entry earned the "unreachable at any setting" verdict for the notation flag alone, and none earned "flag-default-only". Every marked subject that HAS code at HEAD is reached by something: plain batch_analyze (the --joint-inference flag defaults OFF, so the corpus instrument runs the legacy pipeline unless told otherwise), a batch_analyze diagnostic dump flag, or the test suites. A change to any of these subjects still breaks tests and still moves what an untagged batch_analyze run produces. "Dormant" means "not what the product runs", not "nothing runs it".
what_this_found.the_false_negative_enumeration_is_short_: OI-289 enumerates four false-negative paths: an explicit flag flip, batch_analyze without --joint-inference, the test suites, and the declared non-production uncached path. A fifth is load-bearing here: batch_analyze's DIAGNOSTIC DUMP FLAGS, which reach code neither production surface reaches and plain batch_analyze does not either — the Layer-4 slice decoder (--decode-chords) and the whole Layer-5 function module (--dump-l5, --dump-fullspine). ARCHITECTURE.md:1339 already names this path for Layer 3 ("the remaining callers are the batch_analyze diagnostics"); OI-289's list does not.
what_this_found.a_second_flag_gates_reachability: The reachability picture is not one flag. jointKeyWiringEnabled() (regionanalyzer.cpp:1484) is a second runtime flag, default OFF, gating the built half of the shelved joint key-and-chord step INSIDE the legacy arm. A verdict of the form "reachable when the notation flag is flipped" would be wrong for those subjects without also naming this one.
what_this_found.the_largest_transfer_class_was_not_the_p: The largest transfer class — its size is counts.transfer["live-prohibition-in-spec"] above, not typed here (D-431) — is entries restated by a LIVE specification section as standing do-not-retry prohibitions, on the chord layer, the key layer, the search and, since 2026-08-09, the declared mode's weight; docs/redesign_plan.md:4 states the distinction in its own words: "LIVE prohibitions about the legacy chord path". The mark is RIGHT about the subject and the entry still binds what a future designer may attempt. That is a third thing a mark can be, beside "about live code" and "about dead code", and the register has no field for it.
what_this_found.entries_that_describe_an_arrangement_the: Three cases where a reader could take a marked entry for a description of what runs: D-345 (the style preset enters at the key/mode layer — production inference is preset-independent, so on the live arm the preset has no entry point at all), D-351 (the key search is its own decoder — the live estimator decides key and chord in ONE decode), and D-052 (the signature read lives in one shared function — the joint fact adapter does its own). None is a wrong mark. All three are why the mark exists.
what_this_found.no_marked_id_is_cited_anywhere_under_src: The citation scan found not one occurrence of a marked decision ID in any .cpp or .h file. Nothing in the code points back at the decisions that govern it, in either direction, so the transfer half could only ever be searched in prose.
